heading: World News Today Highlights: Tanker hit by drone as US-Iran attacks disrupt Gulf shipping
paragraphs: A tanker carrying nearly 2 million barrels of Iraqi oil was hit by a drone in Iraqi territorial waters on Wednesday, port officials said, as UKMTO reported that several merchant vessels in the Gulf had been hit by disabling fire overnight.
The US military said that it destroyed five Iranian oil tankers on Tuesday (Sep 8) after attacks by Tehran on its warships.

The US Central Command (CENTCOM) in a post on X said, “The CENTCOM forces destroyed five Iranian crude oil carriers, Sept. 8, after the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targeted a U.S. Navy warship with ballistic missiles twice over the past two days.”
CENTCOM said that it destroyed the IRGC crude oil carriers M/T Kaviz, M/T Charminar, M/T Horizon 1, and M/T Riesco in the Gulf of Oman as well as M/T Derya near Kharg Island.

Following the American strikes, Iran launched retaliatory strikes targeting the US bases in Jordan. Jordan’s air-defence systems said that it destroyed 18 of 20 ballistic missiles launched from Iranian territory, the state news agency reported, citing the armed forces. Two projectiles fell in unpopulated areas, and there were no casualties, the news agency reported the military as saying.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned Iran that the United States will continue to launch retaliatory strikes targeting Iranian oil tankers over attempted attacks on US warships.
“Iran continues to try to hit US naval ships, and for every time they do that or try to do that, they’re going to lose tankers,” Rubio told reporters during a visit to Colombia.

Yemen backed Houthis reported over 30 strikes by Saudi on several regions, a day after the militant group launched attacks targeting the neighbouring country, which wounded dozens of people.
“Saudi enemy aircraft launched 32 airstrikes on various areas across the governorates of Marib, Al-Jawf, Taiz and Hodeidah over the past few hours,” the rebels’ Almasirah television said.
The Saudi authorities, on Tuesday (Sep 8), said that Houthi attacks caused temporary shutdowns at oil sites and wounded 73 people.
A policeman was killed and another was injured after unidentified assailants attacked a police patrol team in Pakistan's northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.
The incident took place in the Shatakai Dam area of Karak district.
The police personnel were on patrol duty in the area under the Sabirabad Police Station when the assailants launched the stack.
Constable Zafran was killed in the attack while Constable Muhammad Imtiaz was seriously injured, according to news agency PTI.
The United States banned imports of Canadian alcoholic beverages, motorcycles, and dairy products on Tuesday, escalating the trade war between the two neighbouring nations.
The bans came after Canada imposed retaliatory tariffs on US goods, and will go into effect from September 29.
The Canadian levies followed 50% US tariffs charged on some $20 billion of Canadian goods last month, after multiple rounds of negotiations collapsed.

The breakdown has widened a crack in the bilateral ties between the longtime allies, who have blamed each other for the same. This has prompted Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney to shift away from Canada’s biggest partner in trade, and cast a shadow on the viability of the US-Mexico-Canada agreement.
China has warned the Philippines to stop stirring up trouble and undermining bilateral relations and stability in the South China Sea, while reiterating its position on the arbitration case.

"We advise some people in Philippines to stop trying to stir up trouble, stop undermining bilateral ties and stability in South China Sea," China's foreign ministry said in a note to the Philippine defence chief.
"Don't know the details of the situation, but China's position on South China Sea arbitration case is clear and consistent," the note added.
Russia’s Defence Ministry said a warehouse belonging to a company manufacturing unmanned boats and drones was hit in Kyiv, Interfax reported.
Qatar's Ministry of Interior confirmed that its Civil Defence team brought under control a fire on a marine vessel at Al Wakra Port, with no injuries reported.
"The Civil Defence brings under control a fire on a marine vessel at Al Wakra Port, with no injuries reported," the ministry said in a report on X.

A helicopter carrying Health Ministry personnel crashed in Malaysia’s Sarawak state on Tuesday, killing the pilot and four passengers who were on official duty.

The ministry personnel included a medical officer, an assistant medical officer and two nurses, who were travelling aboard a Flying Doctor Service helicopter, reported the state-run news agency Bernama.

Israel has informed the British consulate in East Jerusalem to close and that the diplomats there will be stripped of their accreditation within 30 days, an Israeli official said, according to Reuters.

Israel further said that British ⁠representatives ⁠assigned to a US-led ⁠Gaza coordination ‌mission ​in Israel, ‌as well as British ‌diplomats based ​in ​Ramallah, ​must leave within ​seven days, Reuters reported, citing the source familiar with the matter.
Israel’s decision to close the British consulate follows sanctions announced by the UK, France and Canada against Israeli settlements, escalating diplomatic tensions.
British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, on Wednesday, said that he regretted Israel's decision to order the consulate ⁠to close, ​but said that it was not surprised.
"We weighed the costs and benefits of acting (...), and we thought we simply could not stand by because we feared Israeli action," he told BBC TV.
Israel informed the British consulate in East Jerusalem that its diplomats will be stripped of their accreditation within 30 days, an Israeli official said, according to Reuters.

Over 1,000 flights in the UK were cancelled on Tuesday due to a technical issue in the air traffic control system, the flight monitoring website Flightradar24 reported. Airports across Britain were witnessing flight delays and cancellations after ​air traffic control ⁠provider NATS experienced ‌a technical glitch.

Air-traffic chiefs said that since planes could not take off safely, departures were severely delayed. Nearly two hours after the air traffic issues persisted across the United Kingdom, the National Air Traffic Control Service (NATS) said engineers had identified the problem and had fixed it, The Independent reported. However, it wasn’t clear how much time it would take for the system to return to normal.

US President Donald Trump hailed what he called a “really big” victory for Germany’s far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD). In a post on his Truth Social handle, he said, " Wow! The Populist Party in Germany just had a really big night. They finally got tired of the absolutely horrible Immigration rules and regulations which have hurt Germany so badly. Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they attacked two US vessels and eight oil tankers in the Gulf in response to what they called a US attack on five Iranian tankers, state media reported citing the group's statement. The group further said that it attacked 1 ships that were attempting to cross "prohibited and unsafe" area of the Strait of Hormuz.
